logp.method_description: The lipophilicity (logarithm of the partition coefficient, log P) of the complexes and photolysis products was measured using the “shake flask” method [56]. PBS buffer was used as an aqueous phase and 1-octanol was used as an organic phase. Prior to the experiments, the PBS solution and octanol were mutually saturated with each other according to the following procedure: 10 ml of octanol was shaken with 1 ml of PBS for 20 min, allowed to settle, and then separated from the PBS using a separatory funnel. An identical procedure was carried out to saturate the PBS solution with octanol. For the measurement, 1·10-4 M solutions of the complexes were prepared in PBS and then mixed with equal volume of 1-octanol (3 ml). The solutions were shaken for 5 min and allowed to settle for 72 h in the dark. The relative distribution of the complexes in the PBS and 1-octanol phases were determined spectrophotometrically. Log P values were calculated using the absorbance of the complexes in 1-octanol divided by the absorbance in water at 300 nm (log P300 = AOctanol/AWater).
